title: The I-power torsion submodule is unchanged by a flat base change that is an isomorphism modulo I
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be a flat ring map of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and $I\subseteq R$ a finitely generated ideal such that the ring map $R/I\to S/IS$ induced by $\varphi$ is an isomorphism ($IS$ the ideal of $S$ generated by $\varphi(I)$). For an $R$-module $P$ put $P[I^\infty]=\{x\in P:\ I^nx=0\text{ for some }n\ge1\}$, a submodule of $P$. Let $M$ be an $R$-module and $M\otimes_RS$ its base change [def-weil-module-base-change], regarded as an $R$-module via $\varphi$ (so $(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ is the set of $y$ with $I^ny=0$ for some $n$, equivalently $(IS)^ny=0$, since $(IS)^n$ is generated by $\varphi(I^n)$). Then $m\mapsto m\otimes1$ maps $M[I^\infty]$ into $(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$, and the resulting map $M[I^\infty]\to(M\otimes_RS)[I^\infty]$ is bijective.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (lemma-neighbourhood-equivalence, line 24301), part (1)

proof.text: Put T = M[I^infty]. The map m -> 1 tensor m is R-linear and restricts to the primary components by Ideal.primaryComponent.map. Every element of T is killed by I^(n+1) for some n: primaryComponent_mem supplies n, and I^(n+1) is contained in I^n. Apply the torsion-module comparison (05E9) to T; construct the compatible ring equivalence R/I -> S/IS with RingEquiv.ofBijective from the assumed bijective quotient map. Tensor symmetry turns the comparison into the bijection T -> S tensor_R T, x -> 1 tensor x.

Flatness makes T.subtype.lTensor S injective (Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap). Its composite with the bijection of step 1 sends x to 1 tensor x in S tensor_R M and is injective. Taking values in the primary component does not alter injectivity.

For a primary-component element y of S tensor_R M, choose n such that I^n kills y. Since I is finitely generated, so is I^n (Ideal.FG.pow). Choose a finite generating set s of I^n and define delta : M -> (s -> M) by delta(m)(a) = a*m. Tensor induction shows that the finite-product equivalence TensorProduct.piRight carries delta.lTensor S(z) to the tuple (a*z) indexed by s. As every a in s belongs to I^n, this tuple is zero for z=y. Injectivity of piRight gives delta.lTensor S(y)=0. Empty s and n=0 are included.

Flatness and tensor right exactness, packaged as Module.Flat.lTensor_exact S, preserve the exact pair ker(delta) -> M -> (s -> M). Consequently y lifts to z in S tensor_R ker(delta). The kernel is contained in T: if delta(m)=0, every generator kills m; Submodule.torsionBySet_eq_torsionBySet_span implies all of I^n kills m, and primaryComponent_mem gives m in T. Tensor the inclusion ker(delta) -> T and obtain a lift in S tensor_R T. The private helper killed_by_fg_lift proves steps 3 and 4 entirely in Lean.

By the surjectivity in step 1 the lift in S tensor_R T is 1 tensor x for some x in T. Tensor functoriality identifies its image with 1 tensor x in S tensor_R M, hence with y. Subtype.ext turns that equality into the required equality of primary-component elements. This proves surjectivity, and step 2 proves injectivity.

proof_origin.place: Adaptation of More on Algebra, Lemma 05EC (1): finite test map and flatness applied to generators of I^n in M, instead of generator powers in M/T; torsion comparison from Lemma 05E9. Source consulted at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05EC.
